title: Heterometallic Lanthanide–Titanium Oxo Clusters: A New Family of Water Oxidation Catalysts

synthesis.procedure: Ti(OiPr)4 (18.0 μL, 0.06 mmol) was added to a solution of 4-tert-butylbenzoate (0.088 g, 0.49 mmol; identified in the main text as Htbba, 4-tert-butylbenzoic acid) and Eu(Ac)3·3H2O (0.0192 g, 0.05 mmol) in 3.0 mL of a CH3CN/THF mixture (3:1) in a glass vial. The solution was stirred for 30 min and heated at approximately 70 °C for 600 min. After cooling to room temperature, colourless rod-shaped crystals formed. The product was washed thoroughly with acetonitrile and dried at 30 °C in a vacuum drying oven for 12 h. Yield 45% based on Eu(Ac)3·3H2O.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Colourless rod-shaped crystals obtained on cooling to room temperature; washed thoroughly with acetonitrile and dried at 30 °C under vacuum for 12 h.

properties.summary: UV/vis diffuse-reflectance spectroscopy gives an optical band gap of 2.90 eV for 1, smaller than the reported 3.2 eV for anatase; the Eu, Sm, and Gd analogues differ slightly in band gap.

synthesis.procedure: Cluster 2 was synthesized in the same manner as 1, replacing Eu(Ac)3·3H2O with Sm(Ac)3·3H2O. The shared procedure uses Ti(OiPr)4 (18.0 μL, 0.06 mmol), 4-tert-butylbenzoate (0.088 g, 0.49 mmol), and the lanthanide acetate hydrate (0.0192 g, 0.05 mmol for the Eu salt) in 3.0 mL of CH3CN/THF (3:1) in a glass vial, stirring for 30 min and heating at approximately 70 °C for 600 min, then cooling to room temperature. The product was washed with acetonitrile and dried at 30 °C under vacuum for 12 h. Yield 40%.
